_comment: Hidden coves that can become bases (scripts/bases.gd). A cove with a "maroons" key is a Maroon landing instead (scripts/maroons.gd): never a base, never spotted by sailing past, only learnt from people. Found by sailing close (your navigator spots them) or through events. shelter: how hard the place is to find and to assault (defence and visibility). soil: whether plantations grow here. water: a spring (garrison needs less food brought in).

ile_a_vache.name: Île-à-Vache
ile_a_vache.description: A low wooded island off Hispaniola's south coast, where Morgan once gathered his fleet. Good water, poor hiding.

isle_of_pines.name: Isle of Pines
isle_of_pines.description: A pine-covered island south of Cuba, ringed by reefs that only a shallow keel can thread.

roatan.name: Roatán
roatan.description: Bay Islands, far from any governor. Deep, hidden bays and a reef that wrecks the unwary.

andros.name: Andros
andros.description: Mangrove creeks on the edge of the Tongue of the Ocean. Nobody comes here who doesn't have to.

saona.name: Saona
saona.description: A flat island off Hispaniola's eastern point, close to the Mona Passage and every ship that uses it.

grand_cayman.name: Grand Cayman
grand_cayman.description: Turtle hunters' island in the middle of the sea between Jamaica and Cuba. Sheltered sound, few visitors.

manchioneal.name: Manchioneal Bay
manchioneal.description: A river mouth on Jamaica's empty east coast, under the Blue Mountains. The Windward Maroons come down here to trade, when they trust the ship.

bahoruco.name: Bahoruco shore
bahoruco.description: A stony beach below the Bahoruco mountains, on Hispaniola's south coast. Up in the forest is Le Maniel, a town of people who escaped the Spanish and French estates, free for longer than anyone remembers.

vieques.name: Vieques
vieques.description: Crab Island, east of Puerto Rico. Spain claims it and never sends anyone.
